:::{#def-global-minimizer}
#### Global minimizer

Let $A \subseteq \reals^p$
and let $f : A \to \reals$ be a [function](sets-functions.qmd#def-function).
A point $x^* \in A$ is a **global minimizer** of $f$ over $A$
if $f(x^*) \le f(x)$ for all $x \in A$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-global-minimizer-argmin}
#### Global minimizers form the argmin

The global minimizers of $f$ are exactly the elements of
$\argmin_{x \in A} f(x)$ (@def-argmin).
A function can have more than one global minimizer.
For example, $f(x) = (x^2 - 1)^2$ on $\reals$
satisfies $f(x) \ge 0$ for every $x$,
and $f(x) = 0$ exactly when $x = -1$ or $x = 1$,
so its global minimizers are $-1$ and $1$,
and $\argmin_{x \in \reals} f(x) = \cb{-1, 1}$.

:::
